task: Social media user influence network analysis (2-source join -> interaction aggregation -> directed weighted graph -> PageRank alpha=0.85 -> top-10 output.csv)

method.join: inner join on username_key = str.strip().str.lower() (User ID ignored); 2694 matched users = node set (twitter-coverage 28.5%)
method.aggregation: per user: mention_count = SUM('Mention Count') over bot rows; follower_count = MAX('Follower Count') (snapshot attribute); retweets_sum/likes_sum = SUM over twitter rows
method.graph: for each target user u in sorted(username_key) order: k = min(mention_count_u, 10); k distinct source users drawn without replacement with probability proportional to follower_count (uniform fallback if zero total); directed edge s -> u
method.edge_weight: mention_count_u / k (mention mass split evenly over in-edges, so a node's total in-weight equals its mention_count)
method.pagerank: power iteration, alpha=0.85, weight='weight', tol=1e-10, max_iter=200 (networkx not installed -> own implementation, networkx-equivalent formulation incl. uniform dangling redistribution); converged in 29 iterations, L1 delta 6.13e-11
method.randomness: numpy.random.default_rng(42) + deterministic sorted node iteration -> fully reproducible

different_seed(7)_same_method.note: sampling noise materially reshuffles the top-10 (mention counts drive in-degree, but which users point in is random); seed 42 is the specified/reported run

notes: Referential/random graph: the only edges are those synthesized from mention counts; there is no observed interaction log linking specific users, so PageRank reflects synthetic attention flow, not verified real interaction.
Inner join restricted to the 2694 users present in both sources (6753 twitter-only and 37872 bot-only users excluded; 28.52% twitter / 6.64% bot coverage); ranking must not be read as global.
10 of the 2694 users are the reported top-10; scores span 0.001811-0.002418 vs uniform baseline 0.000371.
